blocks.text: The speechwriter workflow in Apple Mail
Speechwriting requires long periods of uninterrupted focus. Email often breaks this flow. You need a system that keeps your inbox organized without demanding your constant attention.
Start by using keyboard shortcuts. Press ⌘ N to start a new message. Use ⌘ R to reply. These small habits save minutes every hour. They keep your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the text.
Organizing your inbox for client projects

You likely manage multiple speeches at once. Do not rely on a single inbox. Create smart mailboxes to group messages by client or project name. Go to Mailbox > New Smart Mailbox. Set the criteria to include messages where the subject contains your client name. This keeps your view clean.

When you are deep in a draft, do not switch apps to check an email. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to summarize the latest thread from a client. You get the context without leaving your document. Use this to maintain your creative momentum.

Speech drafts often include high-resolution media or long documents. Apple Mail has a 20 MB limit for standard attachments. If your file is larger, use Mail Drop. It uploads the file to iCloud and sends a link instead. This is automatic when you attach a file larger than the limit.

Writing emails can feel like a chore after a long day of drafting. Hold fn to start dictating your response. Speak naturally. Lazur cleans up the text and formats it at your cursor. This is ideal for quick scheduling or simple feedback acknowledgments.

items: Keeping the inbox open on your second screen. Close it to avoid constant visual interruptions.
Forgetting to use the Flagged mailbox. Use ⌃ ⌘ L to flag important client notes.
Ignoring the search bar. Use ⌘ ⌥ F to search across all mailboxes instantly.
Sending files without checking the size. Always check the attachment size in the status bar.

faq.question: Does Apple Mail support AI features for speechwriters?
faq.answer: Apple Mail includes smart features on Apple Silicon Macs, but for custom drafting and research, many speechwriters use Lazur to handle text and information while keeping their workflow on the Mac.

faq.question: How do I move emails to folders quickly?
faq.answer: You can drag and drop messages into folders in the sidebar. For more speed, use the Message > Move to menu or create a rule to automate this process.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to write my emails?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn while your cursor is in the compose window to dictate your thoughts. Lazur will type out clear, formatted text for you.
